prompt: Write a Python function `top_words(text: str, k: int) -> list[tuple[str, int]]` that returns the k most frequent words in `text` with their counts, most frequent first. A word is a run of ASCII letters and apostrophes; compare case-insensitively and return words in lower case. Break ties alphabetically. Leading and trailing apostrophes are not part of a word ("'hello'" is "hello", but "don't" stays "don't"); a run that is only apostrophes is not a word. If there are fewer than k distinct words, return them all.
